items.title: The truncated second moment of a Gaussian row

source.anchor: Appendix C.2 Ex108 and p12.m5; Ex107 definition; p1/p10, S4.E11 and C.2p5 index conventions
source.attribution: On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling, arXiv:2610.20492v1.
source.scope: Unnormalized retained row second moment and the immediate single-row matrix expectation.

items.statement: At the cutoff \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\), the retained standard-Gaussian second moment is \(aI_r\).

formulae.label: Actual single-row matrix mean
formulae.tex: \begin{aligned}Y_i&=\frac1d(ZZ^\top\otimes t_it_i^\top)\mathbf1_{\{R\le L\}},\\\mathbb E Y_i&=\frac ad(I_r\otimes t_it_i^\top).\end{aligned}

assumptions: Let \(d,q\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(2q+1<d\), and set \(r=q+1\). The case \(q=0\) has \(r=1\).
The row has the canonical law \(Z\sim N(0,I_r)\), with \(R=\|Z\|^2\). Retain the closed event \(R\le L\).

The expectation uses the original Gaussian measure. The coefficient \(a\) is the retained radial moment divided by \(r\). Both matrix integrability conclusions are proved using the Euclidean operator norm.

For the private application use \(\theta_j=(j-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(j=1,\ldots,d\), and \(t_j=(1,\sqrt2\cos\theta_j,\ldots,\sqrt2\cos(q\theta_j))\). Lean uses \(j=i.val+1\) for \(i\in\mathrm{Fin}(d)\) and zero-based feature frequencies.

obligations.label: The Ex108 matrix second moment with the actual p12.m5 consumer.

bindings.boundary: The exact canonical single-row truncated second moment and the actual deterministic-row Y mean are compiled. The original joint row-family pushforward and integral transport, aggregate cosine-frame means, centered bounds, fourth moments, matrix concentration, full Lemma 4.4, both main lower bounds and oracle/precision/cost adapters are separate. Independent source/native review, public integration, complete desktop/mobile reader acceptance and purification are pending.

assumption_deltas.source: A standard r-dimensional Gaussian row, with r=q+1 and the standing source range.
assumption_deltas.lean: The canonical standard Gaussian on EuclideanSpace real Fin(q+1), including q=0 and 2q+1<d.
assumption_deltas.reason: The local theorem realizes the canonical single-row marginal. Original row-family law transport is separate.

assumption_deltas.source: The retained unnormalized matrix expectation equals a I_r.
assumption_deltas.lean: The matrix integrability is also a proved conclusion, using the Euclidean operator norm.
assumption_deltas.reason: The source expectation presupposes finite entries. Scalar and matrix integrability are internal proof components.

assumption_deltas.source: The immediate Y_i mean tensors with the deterministic cosine row and scales by 1/d.
assumption_deltas.lean: The private application uses the literal midpoint cosine feature and derives the expected tensor matrix.
assumption_deltas.reason: The zero-based Fin row maps to the source one-based index by successor. Feature frequencies stay zero-based.
